transcript.text: What’s the main goal you’d like this plan to support?
I want to get back to a comfortable 5K.
When you picture this plan working, what does it look like? For example: start with some easy jogging, then build up to longer runs.
Start with short easy jogs mixed with walking, then slowly build until I can run a whole 5K without stopping.

Your goal, in your words: "I want to get back to a comfortable 5K." Your recorded history covers 180 days. Your longest qualified continuous block is 45.3 minutes. In that time you've recorded 36 runs and 36 walks. None of those runs reached a steady jogging pace yet. Your mix of running and walking shows you’re already building the endurance needed for a comfortable return to race distance. How would you describe where you are with your activity right now?
Yes, that's right. I stopped running a couple of months ago.
Which days and times are you realistically available to run?
Monday, Wednesday and Friday evenings, plus Saturday morning.
What kinds of exercise do you enjoy, and is there anything you’d rather avoid? For example: running and walking, but no gym.
Walking is what I do now, and I'd like to get back to running.
Is there anything we should plan around, like an injury or a health condition?
My right knee gets sore when I ramp up too fast, so I'd like to go easy on it.
I heard: your right knee — keep an eye on it. In your words: “My right knee gets sore when I ramp up too fast, so I'd like to go easy on it.” Is that right? Say yes or correct it.

constraints.text: My right knee gets sore when I ramp up too fast, so I'd like to go easy on it.

transcript.text: Yes, that's right.
How would you like me to communicate with you—plain, warm, or terse, and brief or full?
Warm and brief.
Here's how the plan will run: we check in every Sunday, and I plan 4 weeks at a time, always looking about 12 weeks ahead. Does that work, or would you like to change anything?
Sunday check-ins, 4 weeks at a time.
